items.title: Gucci Price Cuts Break Luxury's Biggest Taboo. Louis Vuitton Is Weighing It
items.summary: Forbes reports Gucci has cut prices on handbags (its crystal Padlock top-handle bag down roughly 30% in France, from EUR 3,500 to EUR 2,450) amid 13 consecutive quarters of sales declines, a reversal that Bernstein analyst Luca Solca flagged as unprecedented. Barclays analyst Carole Madjo is quoted questioning whether shoppers should keep buying if prices keep falling, while Goldman's Erwan Rambourg argues the deeper problem is lost brand identity, not price; Louis Vuitton is reportedly weighing but resisting matching cuts since aspirational shoppers are over half of both brands' sales -- directly relevant to SEA's price-sensitive aspirational luxury segment.

items.title: 구찌 가방 95만원 내렸다...콧대 높던 명품업계에 무슨 일이 (Gucci cuts bag price by KRW 950,000)
items.summary: Hankyung reports Gucci lowered its Mercato small tote by 21.3% (KRW 4.45m to KRW 3.5m) and the Padlock crystal bag by about 30% in France, the first double-digit luxury price cut in the region since Chanel's 2015 adjustment -- a milestone the piece frames as luxury industry capitulation after prolonged soft demand, with LVMH's CFO confirming internal discussion of matching cuts. Included here for Greater-China-diaspora/regional-luxury-market relevance per this system's SEA convention, since Korean coverage closely tracks the pan-Asian pricing debate affecting SEA shoppers who cross-shop.

items.title: Gucci, Prada close more China outlets as consumers cut luxury spending
items.summary: SCMP (Hong Kong, pan-Asia reach including SEA Chinese-diaspora readers) reports Gucci and Prada have shuttered additional mainland China outlets as shoppers pull back, part of Kering's plan to close roughly 125 net stores by end of 2026; Asia-Pacific excluding Japan still accounts for over a third of Gucci revenue, but Chinese consumers increasingly buy abroad or simply spend less, a trend with direct spillover into SEA tourist-retail markets (Singapore, Bangkok) that depend on Chinese luxury tourism.

items.title: Gucci to Stage Cruise 2028 Show in Shanghai
items.summary: WWD confirms creative director Demna will stage Gucci's Cruise 2028 show in Shanghai on May 17, 2027, marking the 30th anniversary of the brand's first China store; framed as a bid to rebuild ties with Chinese clientele who have pulled back on spending for macroeconomic and cultural reasons. Relevant to SEA as a signal of Gucci doubling down on Greater China/Asia-Pacific engagement rather than retreating, with likely regional VIP and ambassador spillover into Southeast Asian markets.

items.title: Mariah Carey Stars in Gucci's 2026 Christmas Campaign
items.summary: Mariah Carey fronts Gucci's 2026 holiday campaign film, 'Gucci Gift with Mariah Carey,' directed by Harmony Korine and set to 'All I Want for Christmas Is You,' showcasing the new Butterfly collection alongside Starlet, Marmont and Paparazzo bags; released on Gucci's YouTube channel. Pure activation/brand-marketing coverage with no independent critical angle, included to track volume of the week's dominant Gucci marketing story that is also circulating across SEA entertainment press and social feeds.

items.title: Fans Are 'Disappointed' Over Mariah Carey's 'Depressing' Gucci Holiday Campaign & 'Boring' Styling
items.summary: Aggregated social reaction piece reports viewers calling the Gucci-Mariah Carey holiday film 'sterile, cold, and devoid of humanity' and 'outdated' despite the upbeat soundtrack, with some fans specifically criticizing the styling as boring; a minority of commenters pushed back, praising Carey's personal looks. A rare instance of genuine, unprompted negative public reaction to a Gucci activation rather than pure promotional coverage.

items.title: Gucci giam gia, nhung nguoi tieu dung lieu co quay lai? (Gucci cuts prices, but will consumers come back?)
items.summary: Vietnamese luxury-lifestyle outlet Luxuo covers Gucci's price cuts and surveys Vietnamese consumer sentiment directly: of 15 respondents, 7 said they would buy now, 5 said they would wait for prices to drop further, and 3 said Gucci remains too expensive regardless; a separate LuxIntel Think Tank poll found 22 of 28 participants believe Gucci should lower prices further. Concludes that price cuts alone may not restore the brand's appeal, a skeptical read directly from the Vietnamese market.

items.title: 古驰Gucci突然降价最高40%，是抄底时机还是品牌降级？ (Gucci suddenly cuts prices up to 40% - bargain window or brand downgrade?)
items.summary: A Weibo long-post (reaching Greater-China-diaspora audiences who heavily overlap with SEA Chinese-Singaporean/Malaysian/Indonesian luxury shoppers) frames Gucci's steep markdowns -- Ophidia mini bucket bag down over 40%, Mercato tote down to RMB 20,000 -- as a live debate between 'bottom-fishing opportunity' and 'brand devaluation,' citing secondhand resale anchors dropping roughly 27-29% in sympathy and contrasting Gucci's weak value retention against Hermes and Chanel. Directly captures the ambivalent-to-negative public read on the pricing reset that official PR frames positively.

items.title: Vogue Thailand on Demna's 'Store Show' runway concept
items.summary: Vogue Thailand's X account covers Demna's 'The Store Show' runway concept where models walked as if shopping customers inside a store set, a format break from convention; post is descriptive fashion-editorial coverage aimed at the Thai fanbase with no independent critical assessment, but signals continued strong SEA media engagement with Demna-era Gucci runway output.

items.title: Harper's Bazaar Thailand on Gulf Kanawut's year as Gucci ambassador
items.summary: Harper's Bazaar Thailand's X account quotes Thai actor and Gucci brand ambassador Gulf Kanawut thanking fans for a year of effort and growth as a brand face; short celebratory fan/ambassador post, pure activation coverage with no critical content, illustrative of the steady drip of ambassador-driven SEA social volume for Gucci.

items.title: Gucci Just Won Christmas With A Holiday Campaign Starring Mariah Carey
items.summary: PurseBlog's handbag-community commentary gives a strongly positive take on the Mariah Carey holiday campaign, calling it a clear win for Gucci's seasonal marketing and highlighting the Butterfly collection pieces; useful as a counterweight data point to the Yahoo-aggregated fan backlash item, showing opinion among core handbag-community readers is split rather than uniformly negative.

items.title: WWD TikTok recap of Gucci Cruise show front row and Demna succession context
items.summary: WWD's TikTok account recaps a recent Gucci Cruise collection presentation at Palazzo Settimanni with front-row guests Paul Mescal and Julia Garner, using the clip to recap the creative-director handover context (studio-team design following Sabato De Sarno's exit, ahead of Demna's arrival); descriptive editorial recap repurposed for TikTok's short-video audience, part of the steady SNS volume around Gucci's creative-direction narrative that SEA youth audiences consume on the platform.

collector_notes.freshness: All 12 admitted items are dated 2026-11-09 through 2026-11-17, inside the 72h-to-7-day target window (TikTok/PurseBlog items run to the edge of the acceptable 7-day band). Several promising SEA-specific leads (Gucci Cruise 2026 Greenbelt/Manila preview with Helm restaurant, Billkin x Gucci Marina Bay Sands event, Davika Hoorne Thailand ambassadorship) were investigated and REJECTED after verification showed their actual publish dates were November-December 2025, over a year stale, despite search snippets ambiguously implying November 2026 -- a reminder that SEA search results heavily recycle prior-year seasonal/ambassador content under similar headlines.
collector_notes.anti_bias_balance: Critical-angle searches (price hike/cut backlash, resale value drop, store closures, earnings miss, 'lost its way') were run in English, Korean, Chinese, Thai and Vietnamese and were NOT dry this cycle -- they surfaced the week's dominant real story (Gucci's ~30-40% price cuts across markets) plus consumer skepticism in Vietnam (luxuo.vn survey), China/diaspora resale-value anxiety (Weibo), fan backlash to the Mariah Carey campaign (Yahoo aggregation), and continued China store closures (SCMP). The pool is therefore more balanced than prior days: roughly half the items (Forbes, Hankyung, SCMP, luxuo.vn, Weibo, Yahoo-fan-backlash) carry a critical or skeptical angle, while the other half (WWD Shanghai announcement, Mariah Carey campaign, ambassador/runway SNS posts, PurseBlog) are activation coverage or genuinely positive community reaction.
collector_notes.channel_mix: News=6, sns=4 (Weibo, 2x X, TikTok), community=1 (PurseBlog) for a total of 11 non-duplicate source-type items across 12 entries. The >=3 sns/community target was met (5 combined). Community coverage remains the weakest channel: Pantip, Kaskus, Lowyat, HardwareZone and Webtretho were all checked in-language (Thai/Indonesian/Vietnamese/English) but returned only off-topic, stale (pre-2026), or unrelated shopping-recommendation threads with no fresh Gucci-specific discussion -- this is a genuine dry result, not a search-effort gap.
collector_notes.volume: 12 vetted items this cycle, below the >=25 target (>=8 news/>=8 sns/>=6 community) but a meaningful improvement on the prior day's 3-item pool, driven mainly by the fresh, high-volume Gucci price-cut story cycle (Nov 13-17) rather than brand-initiated activation, which this run deliberately did not pad with stale filler.
